claims.text: Sequence-level probability estimates given by LLMs have limitations as reliable indicators of generation quality.
LLMs demonstrate strong calibration at the token level for multiple-choice questions.
LLMs demonstrate strong calibration at the token level for evaluating true/false statements.
Self-evaluation based scores improve accuracy in selective generation tasks.
Self-evaluation based scores correlate better with the overall quality of generated content than likelihood-based metrics.
Open-ended generation tasks can be reformulated into token-level prediction tasks to leverage LLM calibration.

evidence.description: Experiments with PaLM-2 and GPT-3 on TruthfulQA and TL;DR benchmarks demonstrate improved accuracy.
Self-evaluation scores correlate better with the overall quality of generated content in PaLM-2 and GPT-3 experiments.

methodologies.name: Self-Evaluation Scoring
methodologies.description: Instructing an LLM to evaluate its own answers using multi-way comparison or point-wise evaluation reformulated as token-level prediction.

limitations.text: Sequence-level probability estimates (e.g., perplexity) are unreliable indicators of generation quality.
